description:
Advances: ancora.derive
Ready-for: implement
Severity: High (calibrated; critical review 2026-09-05, consolidated CF9, spec H1).

Symptom: surface: [] in a subject spec-meta is truthy, so Gate.subject_surface/2 returns [] and every binding of that subject becomes derived/drift_transitive at info; mix spec.check reports errors=0 with no reason recorded and no acknowledged label.
Evidence: ancora.derive.drift_primary_transitive enumerates three cases and stops before the empty list; reproduced on a probe index. Also undefined: whether an entry is an exact repo-relative path, a prefix, or a glob.
Why now: a one-line spec-meta edit silently downgrades a whole subject. Questions: does an empty list mean absent or everything-transitive (recommend: reject with a spec finding); what is the match rule. Then implement, test, and finish the docs ancora-gg8.9 started. Related: ancora-btu.

## Investigation contract, 2026-09-07

Evidence and corrections:
Report: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/04-report.md
Measurements: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/03-measurements.md
Source revision: 82c2ca8329e1303ececc610dfc9f72986b96c84a. This contract proposes work; no implementation is claimed.

Deliverable:
Define surface as a nonempty list of exact, canonical project-relative file paths. Reject empty, absolute, traversal, empty-component, dot-component and glob entries with an invalid spec finding; never interpret them as all-transitive. Allow spaces and Unicode. Do not require a path to exist on HEAD, since a deleted or moved source path can be legitimate base ownership. Absence retains conservative primary classification. Update schema, examples and contracts. For existing drift classification, use ownership on either side when both sides declare a surface; removing surface restores conservative behavior. First introduction uses the explicit HEAD declaration and must be displayed as an ownership-policy change in review. Unknown defining paths remain primary.

Verification:
- surface: [] is rejected, valid exact paths accepted, prefixes do not match descendants, and glob syntax is rejected.
- A changed definition owned on either declared side remains primary even when its entry is removed in the same diff. With surface absent on HEAD, every observed drift remains primary.
- First introduction is visible as a policy change and outside-surface drift is informational. Unknown locations stay primary. A stale deleted path is accepted as an exact declaration, not treated as evidence of tested coverage.
- Cadence: focused tests during implementation; at final verification run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix test, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused and mix spec.check against the actual integration base. CI must pass both configured Elixir/OTP combinations. Record evidence of the described symptom after the consuming release before claiming it done.

Allowed touches:
lib/ancora/schema/meta.ex, parser validation, lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex, review policy display, relevant tests, ancora.derive/parsing/review specs and decision amendment.

Out of Scope (files):
Unrelated production modules, credentials, dependencies and consumer repositories. Release metadata belongs to release preparation.

Out of Scope (intent):
No mandatory adoption of surfaces, inferred ownership, directory/glob semantics, or surface-based coverage claims. Growth/shrink extension belongs to the primary attribution contract.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Focused negative and positive behavior fixtures pass.
- [ ] Affected specs and decisions describe the actual changed behavior.
- [ ] Full repository CI and spec gate pass without cosmetic acknowledgment edits.

Decision:
Reject the empty-list bypass and make path matching explicit. The measured accepted empty list silently routes everything to transitive. Exact matching keeps the declaration reviewable.

Open Questions:
None. Unmeasured consumer replay and release behavior are explicit Verification obligations, not claimed results.
title: Define surface: semantics: empty list, path matching, and documentation
